title: Composition of exceptional direct images
statement:
For composable separated finite-type morphisms
$X_0\xrightarrow fY_0\xrightarrow gZ_0$ of separated finite-type
$k_0$-schemes, the exceptional direct images satisfy a functorial
isomorphism $R(gf)_!\simeq Rg_!Rf_!$ compatible with Frobenius.

proof.text: Use the global finite-field and coefficient conventions: $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, $k=\overline{k_0}$ and $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k_0)$. Write $X,Y,Z,f,g$ for the geometric fibers of the given schemes and morphisms. By [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change], these are separated finite-type $k$-schemes and separated finite-type morphisms, so they satisfy the geometric hypotheses of [prop-functor-package]. The composite $gf$ is the geometric fiber of $g_0f_0$, and the composition clause is stated for the pair $f,g$ of such morphisms. The coefficient category is $D^b_c(-,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)=\mathcal C_{(-)}$, the common-stage category of [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]: it is the category on which the functors $Rf_!$ of [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support] act, the $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ stage of the package's datum, and the base of the Weil categories of [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. The pair-category notation of [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category] in the statement dependencies is not identified with it anywhere in this proof. On $\mathcal C_{(-)}$, clause (3) of the package supplies a natural isomorphism $\beta:R(gf)_!\xrightarrow{\sim}Rg_!Rf_!$. Its opening preservation assertion ensures that $Rf_!K$ is again a bounded constructible input for $Rg_!$. This applies the field-stage clause itself; it does not identify discrete non-torsion etale coefficients with the completed and transported coefficient category.

proof.text: Equip each compact-support image with its canonical Weil structure by [lem-fix-weil-operations]. Its explicit assertion that composition comparisons are equivariant applies to the comparison $\beta$ from step 1: all morphisms are defined over $k_0$, the coefficient is $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, and bounded constructibility was checked in step 1. For a Weil complex $(K,\theta_K)$, write $\theta_A$ for the resulting structure on $A=R(gf)_!K$ and $\theta_B$ for the iterated structure on $B=Rg_!Rf_!K$. With $F_Z^*$ denoting geometric-Frobenius pullback, equivariance is $\beta_K\theta_A=\theta_B F_Z^*(\beta_K)$. This is exactly the morphism condition in [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. Composing that equality with $\beta_K^{-1}$ on the left and $F_Z^*(\beta_K^{-1})$ on the right gives $\beta_K^{-1}\theta_B=\theta_A F_Z^*(\beta_K^{-1})$, so the inverse also is a Weil morphism. Naturality of $\beta$ restricts to Weil morphisms because the operations act on their underlying maps. Thus $\beta$ is the required functorial Frobenius-compatible isomorphism.
